name: Primary Non-Gestational Choriocarcinoma of Ovary

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Immunohistochemical Diagnostic Criteria for Primary Non-Gestational Ovarian Choriocarcinoma

criteria.description: Presence of biphasic population of cytotrophoblasts and syncytiotrophoblasts without villous structures on histopathology
Marked elevation of serum beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG) levels in absence of pregnancy
Exclusion of gestational origin by clinical history and absence of intrauterine or extrauterine pregnancy
Positive immunohistochemical staining for β-hCG and cytokeratin markers in tumor tissue
Ovarian mass detected on imaging with no evidence of uterine or extraovarian primary gestational tumor

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of choriocarcinoma in ovarian tissue with elevated β-hCG and exclusion of gestational origin
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular genetic testing may assist in differentiating gestational from non-gestational origin.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Marked serum beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG) elevation
pathognomonic.notes: Key tumor marker for diagnosis and monitoring
searchTerms: high blood levels of pregnancy hormone

pathognomonic.notes: Palpable adnexal mass on physical exam

pathognomonic.symptomName: Histopathological identification of cytotrophoblasts and syncytiotrophoblasts without villi

common.notes: Due to tumor mass effect or hemorrhage
searchTerms: pain in lower abdomen or pelvis

common.notes: Secondary to tumor burden or paraneoplastic effects
Due to peritoneal irritation or metastasis

searchTerms: shortness of breath due to lung tumors
dyspnea caused by cancer spread to lungs

occasional.notes: Due to β-hCG cross-reactivity with TSH receptor

searchTerms: brain lesions causing weakness or numbness

laboratory: Markedly elevated serum beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG)
Possible thyroid function abnormalities due to β-hCG cross-reactivity
imaging: Ultrasound showing unilateral ovarian mass with heterogeneous echotexture
CT/MRI demonstrating ovarian tumor without uterine involvement
Chest imaging revealing pulmonary metastases in advanced cases
genetic: Molecular analysis differentiating gestational from non-gestational origin via DNA polymorphism studies
other: Histopathology showing biphasic trophoblastic cell populations without chorionic villi
Immunohistochemical positivity for β-hCG and cytokeratin

distinguishingFeatures: History of recent pregnancy or molar pregnancy
Presence of intrauterine or extrauterine gestational tissue
Genetic analysis showing paternal DNA contribution
Presence of mixed germ cell tumor components
Different histopathological features without trophoblastic differentiation

redFlags: Rapidly rising serum β-hCG without evidence of pregnancy
Unilateral adnexal mass with hemorrhagic or necrotic features
Signs of metastatic spread such as hemoptysis or neurological deficits
references: Scully RE. Tumors of the ovary and maldeveloped gonads. Atlas of Tumor Pathology, 2nd Series, Fascicle 23. Armed Forces Institute of Pathology; 1979.
